Facts;Invertebrates;Giant Anteater Facts;The giant anteater lives up to its name: it is large and eats ants. In fact, giant anteaters are the largest species of anteater. Giant anteaters can grow to be 1.8-2.4 meters (6-8 ft.) from nose to tail and weigh between 25-45 kg (55-100 lb.). Males and females are roughly the same size. Found all over Central and South America, except for Guatemala, Uruguay, and El Salvador, giant anteaters live in a variety of habitats such as forests, wetlands, savannas, and grasslands. They keep a range of 1.5 to 2.5 km (1-1.5 mi.). Giant anteaters do not have a den and rest in many places within their range.;

Spider;Invertebrates;Giant House Spider;France, Belgium, Netherlands, Germany, Switzerland, Austria, Czech Republic, Poland, Denmark, Sweden The giant house spider (Eratigena atrica) is a large European funnel-weaver often found in buildings and outbuildings. Carp;Invertebrates;Grass Carp;Grass carp (Ctenopharyngodon idella) is a large freshwater minnow (family Cyprinidae) native to eastern Asia, widely introduced elsewhere—often for aquatic vegetation control. Aphids;Invertebrates;Green Aphids;Aphids (true aphids) are small sap-feeding insects (Hemiptera) that often form dense colonies on leaves and stems. Many species are green, leading to the common garden term 'green aphids'. They feed with piercing-sucking mouthparts, excrete honeydew, and can transmit numerous plant viruses. Sex differences vary in Aphididae because they often have cycles of asexual reproduction and many forms. For much of the season most are asexual females (often wingless), so sexes may be absent, when sexual forms appear, males and egg-laying females differ. Most Aphididae have cornicles (tailpipe-like tubes) that can release defensive droplets and alarm chemicals. Many species can reproduce without mating for multiple generations, letting colonies explode in days.;

Hallucigenia;Invertebrates;Hallucigenia;Hallucigenia is a small, soft-bodied Cambrian fossil animal known for paired dorsal spines and multiple lobopod (stumpy) legs. It is a key taxon in discussions of early panarthropod evolution and the origins of modern velvet worms/arthropods. Hallucigenia was famously reconstructed upside down at first-its spines were mistaken for walking legs. Multiple species are known from different Cambrian sites of exceptional preservation, especially the Burgess Shale (Canada) and the Chengjiang Biota (China). It's a classic "stem-group panarthropod": close to the evolutionary roots of velvet worms (onychophorans) and arthropods.;

Hermit crabs are anomuran decapod crustaceans best known for occupying empty gastropod shells (or other shelters) to protect their soft, asymmetrical abdomen. Inchworm;Invertebrates;Inchworm;Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, Chile, China, Germany, Egypt, Spain, France, United Kingdom, Indonesia, India, Italy, Japan, Kenya, South Korea, Morocco, Mexico, Malaysia, Nigeria, Norway, New Zealand, Philippines, Poland, Russia, Sweden, Thailand, Turkey, United States, Vietnam, South Africa "Inchworm" isn't a species-it's the larval stage of many of the ~23,000+ geometer moth species worldwide. Inchworms are the caterpillar (larval) stage of geometer moths (Geometridae). They are named for their characteristic “looping” movement: lacking mid-abdominal prolegs, they bring the rear end forward to form a loop, then extend the front end—often described as measuring or “inching” along. Many are excellent twig mimics and may hold themselves stiffly at an angle when disturbed. Inchworm (Geometridae) caterpillars usually cannot be told male or female by appearance, sexing needs a close check of genital openings or rearing. Many adult geometrid moths show sex differences after metamorphosis, which vary by species or subfamily.;

Adult size: head-body 25-36 cm, tail 26-36 cm, total length ~51-72 cm, mass ~1.5-2.0 kg (field guides/IUCN accounts report these ranges). Its coat can look "painted"-deep maroon/brown, black, cream, and rufous patches vary by region and subspecies across peninsular India. It builds large spherical leaf-and-twig nests ("dreys"), often high in the canopy, individuals commonly maintain multiple nests within a home area (documented in Western Ghats field studies).;

Insects;Invertebrates;Insects;All insects are part of the taxonomical phylum Arthropoda, and they are collectively referred to as arthropods. It is common… All insects are part of the taxonomical phylum Arthropoda, and they are collectively referred to as arthropods. It is common to see this name misspelled as “anthropod,” but this is not the correct term. They can be found in nearly every environment on the planet, and they currently account for over half of all known living organisms in the world. They have undergone many cycles of evolution depending on the resources available to them. With over one million described species currently living, and millions more estimated to exist, insects greatly outnumber all other animals. In general, this classification of creatures is referred to as Insecta. In some cases, the terms “Ectognatha” and “Entomida” may be used instead, but these three labels are synonymous and may be used interchangeably. For simplicity, this guide will always use the classification Insecta.;
Pillars;Invertebrates;International Fund For Animal Welfare Continues Work Across Two Pillars;When it was founded by Welsh activist Brian Davies in 1969, the International Fund for Animal Welfare (IFAW) had one primary mission: ending the commercial hunting of whitecoat harp seals and pups on the east coast of Canada. In the nearly six decades since forming, the IFAW has expanded to cover a broader scope of wildlife conservation efforts spanning habitat protection, disaster response, anti-poaching, illegal trade, wildlife rescue and rehabilitation, and fostering human and wildlife cohabitation across 40 countries. Today, there are 328 staff members working for the IFAW across 16 offices worldwide in veterinary, field research and operations, policy, and organizational support, along with wildlife rehabilitators and care technicians, marine rescue and stranding officers, and biologists. “I think as long as you have the passion for animals, there are so many different skill sets that are needed at IFAW to execute our mission,” says Danielle Kessler, Director at the U.S. office of IFAW, who oversees policy and campaign management.;

A miniature (true bantam) ornamental chicken breed originating in Japan, known for very short legs, an upright tail carriage, and a compact body form. In Japanese Bantams, dimorphism is accentuated by the male's more dramatic upright tail and flowing feathers, while both sexes retain the breed's very short legs and compact body. Spider;Invertebrates;Jumping Spider;Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, Chile, China, Colombia, Germany, Egypt, Spain, Fiji, France, United Kingdom, Indonesia, India, Italy, Japan, Kenya, South Korea, Mexico, Malaysia, Nigeria, Norway, New Zealand, Peru, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Portugal, Russia, Sweden, Thailand, Turkey, United States, Vietnam, South Africa Salticidae is the largest spider family, with 6,000+ described species and many more likely undescribed. Jumping spiders (family Salticidae) are a large, diverse group of spiders characterized by active hunting, agile jumping, and exceptional vision. They do not rely on capture webs to catch prey, instead they stalk and pounce, anchoring themselves with a safety dragline of silk. Sexual dimorphism in Salticidae is common but varies. Deer;Invertebrates;Key Deer;The Key deer is the smallest North American deer and an insular subspecies of the white-tailed deer, occurring naturally only in the lower Florida Keys. Sexual dimorphism is present but subtle compared with many deer: bucks are larger and grow antlers, does are smaller and antlerless. This is typical of white-tailed deer, including the Key deer subspecies. Adult size is markedly smaller than mainland white-tailed deer: typical adult mass ≈20-34 kg (♀ ~20-25 kg, ♂ ~25-34 kg) reported in agency/species accounts (e.g., USFWS, FWC). Beetle;Invertebrates;Khapra Beetle;The khapra beetle (Trogoderma granarium) is a small dermestid beetle notorious worldwide as a highly destructive stored-grain and stored-product pest, it is a major quarantine species in many countries. Larvae are the main damaging stage, adults feed little or not at all and live only about 1-2 weeks under warm conditions (stored-product entomology texts, EPPO datasheets). Female fecundity is typically on the order of ~50-100 eggs over her short life (commonly reported ranges in CABI/FAO-style datasheets, varies with temperature and diet). Development speed is highly temperature-dependent: around a month in hot conditions but many months when cool, larvae can also enter diapause and persist in storage structures (EPPO/CABI).;

Crab;Invertebrates;King Crab;Argentina, Australia, Canada, Chile, China, Spain, France, United Kingdom, Greenland, Ireland, Iceland, Japan, South Korea, Mexico, Norway, New Zealand, Portugal, Russia, Taiwan, United States, South Africa "King crab" is a family-level common name (Lithodidae), not a single species-red, golden, and blue king crabs are just a few well-known examples. King crabs are large, often spiny, bottom-dwelling decapod crustaceans in the family Lithodidae. Despite their crab-like form, they are anomuran crustaceans (closer to hermit crabs than to true crabs) and many lineages show strong “carcinization” (evolution toward a crab-like body plan). Several species are major seafood resources in cold-temperate to subpolar seas. Sexual dimorphism is common but variable: males typically grow larger with more robust chelae and longer legs. Females usually have a broader abdomen for brooding eggs and may show different spine robustness or body proportions.;

A Labradane is a hybrid domestic dog produced by crossing a Labrador Retriever with a Great Dane. Individuals often combine a large/giant build with a short coat and a temperament that may blend the Labrador’s gregariousness with the Great Dane’s generally calm demeanor. Ant;Invertebrates;Leafcutter Ant;Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Belize, Colombia, Costa Rica, Cuba, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guatemala, Guyana, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, Panama, Peru, Paraguay, Suriname, El Salvador, Trinidad and Tobago, United States, Venezuela Across Atta, workers don't eat most of the leaves they cut-they use them as compost to feed a cultivated fungus. Atta leafcutter ants are social ants famous for cutting vegetation to cultivate a symbiotic fungus as their primary food source. Colonies can be extremely large and highly organized, with specialized worker castes. Sexual dimorphism is pronounced in winged reproductives: queens are much larger and more robust with enlarged thorax for flight muscles. Lystrosaurus;Invertebrates;Lystrosaurus;Lystrosaurus is an extinct genus of stout-bodied, herbivorous dicynodont therapsids (synapsids) that lived around the Permian–Triassic boundary. It is famous for its abundance in Early Triassic sediments and is often used as an indicator of post-extinction ecological recovery. Fossils are so abundant in some Early Triassic rocks that Lystrosaurus is often called a classic "disaster taxon." Many species had a horny beak for cropping plants, some also carried a pair of tusks, while others show reduced or absent tusks. Lystrosaurus fossils occur across former Gondwana (e.g., southern Africa, India, Antarctica), making the genus important in discussions of ancient continental connections.;

Maggot;Invertebrates;Maggot;Maggots are the soft-bodied, legless larval stage of many true flies (order Diptera). They are primarily adapted for feeding and growth, often in decaying organic matter (saprophagous) but in some groups they are parasitic (causing myiasis) or specialized to particular substrates (e.g., carrion, dung, plant tissue). Diptera (true fly) larvae range in length from about 0.1 cm (1 mm) in very small midges (such as some gall midges) up to about 5 cm in the largest crane fly larvae. Some larvae are aquatic and breathe through rear spiracles, "rat-tailed maggots" (hoverflies) use a snorkel-like tube. Bloodworms (chironomid midge larvae) can be red because they contain hemoglobin-like pigments that help in low-oxygen mud.;

Mealybugs are small, soft-bodied scale insects that feed on plant sap and are typically covered in a white, powdery/waxy secretion. Sexual dimorphism is strong: females are wingless, oval, wax-covered sap feeders, while males are small, slender, usually winged, and short-lived. Males often do not feed as adults and mainly locate females for mating. Most mealybugs are only ~0.8-7 mm long as adult females, yet heavy infestations can stunt or kill large plants.;

Mollusk;Invertebrates;Mollusk;Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, Chile, China, Egypt, Spain, France, United Kingdom, Indonesia, India, Italy, Japan, Kenya, South Korea, Morocco, Mexico, Norway, New Zealand, Peru, Philippines, Russia, Sweden, Thailand, United States, South Africa Size spans extremes: minute snails under 1 mm across, while the largest squids reach roughly 10-13 m in total length. Mollusks (phylum Mollusca) are a major group of invertebrate animals that includes snails and slugs (gastropods), clams and mussels (bivalves), squids and octopuses (cephalopods), chitons (polyplacophorans), and several smaller lineages. Nematode;Invertebrates;Nematode;They may be the most numerous multicellular animals on Earth, occurring in soils, sediments, freshwater, oceans, and inside plants and animals. Nematodes (phylum Nematoda) are unsegmented, cylindrical “roundworms” found in nearly all environments, including soil, freshwater, marine habitats, and as parasites of animals and plants. They are among the most abundant multicellular animals on Earth, ranging from microscopic free-living species to large internal parasites. Sexual dimorphism is common but variable: males are often smaller with a curved tail and copulatory spicules (sometimes a bursa), while females are frequently larger and more fecund. Some groups show minimal external differences or alternative reproductive modes. They may be the most numerous multicellular animals on Earth, occurring in soils, sediments, freshwater, oceans, and inside plants and animals.;
Pigeon;Invertebrates;Nicobar pigeon;India, Myanmar, Thailand, Malaysia, Brunei Darussalam, Indonesia, Philippines, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands The Nicobar pigeon is a large, primarily ground-foraging island pigeon notable for its iridescent green and copper plumage, white tail, and shaggy hackles on the neck. It is the only living species in the genus Caloenas and is closely associated with small islands across the eastern Indian Ocean and western Pacific. It's the only extant species in the genus Caloenas-its closest relatives are extinct island pigeons like the dodo lineage (molecular phylogenies: Shapiro et al., 2002, Pereira et al., 2007). Unlike many tree-perching pigeons, it does much of its feeding on the ground, often on remote predator-free islets.;

The Norway rat (Rattus norvegicus), also called the brown rat, is a large murid rodent native to northern China/Mongolia region but now cosmopolitan, closely associated with human settlements. It is a major commensal species and a common model organism in biomedical research. Males are typically larger and heavier with broader heads/neck and conspicuous testes. Females are generally smaller and show prominent nipples when breeding/lactating, otherwise coat coloration is similar between sexes.;

Females are smaller and lighter-boned, often appearing more refined while retaining the same coat type and tufting. Animals;Invertebrates;Ocean Animals;Ocean animals list for kids (and adults) with pictures and facts. Discover amazing animals that live in the ocean. The ocean covers almost three-quarters of the Earth’s surface and is one of the most important animal habitats. It is home to around 230,000 recorded species , and many more that are still to be discovered and named. Biologists estimate that the total number of species living in the world’s oceans may be over 1,000,000! Wildlife;Invertebrates;ProtectingEndangered Wildlife;Explore animals by their IUCN conservation status. Learn about species facing extinction and discover what makes each category unique. A-Z Animals follows the International Union for the Conservation of Nature (IUCN) ’s nine categories of endangered animal lists. They are the following: The IUCN is the organization that monitors the conservation status and other ecological metrics for the world’s plants and animals. Its mission is to promote sustainable use of the Earth’s resources. Founded in 1948 in Fontainebleau, France, as the Union for the Protection of Nature, the IUCN is the oldest global environmental advocacy group. Today, headquartered in Gland, Switzerland, the umbrella organization collaborates with more than 1,000 smaller nonprofits, associations, and governments representing 140 countries. The IUCN monitors the world’s species, which raises the question: How many species currently live on the planet? In 2016, researchers declared their collective belief that there are more than one trillion species on the Earth. However, scientists have only observed and described about one-thousandth of one percent of them, or 7 to 10 million. The typical lifespan of a species is 10 million years. However, some stick around for hundreds of millions of years. For example, jellyfish have lived on Earth for nearly 550 million years!;

Kids;Invertebrates;Rabbit Facts for Kids;With their long ears and fluffy white tails, rabbits are pretty recognizable. You’ve probably seen one in the wild, or maybe you even have a pet bunny! But did you know there are 29 species of rabbits worldwide? Rabbits vary greatly in size. The smallest rabbit, the pygmy rabbit, is only about 24 cm (9.3 in.) long and 375 g (.8 lb.) in weight. The largest rabbit on record is a Continental Giant breed of domestic rabbit named Darius. He is 1.3 m (4.3 ft.) long and weighs over 23 kg (50 lb.)! Typically, wild rabbits have agouti-colored (brown-gray) fur. But some species are black, like the Amami rabbit in Japan, or black-striped, like the Sumatran striped rabbit or the Annamite striped rabbit in southeast Asia.;
Red;Invertebrates;Red;United Kingdom, Ireland, France, Spain, Portugal, Belgium, Netherlands, Luxembourg, Germany, Switzerland, Austria, Italy, Denmark, Norway, Sweden, Finland, Poland, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary, Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, Montenegro, Albania, Macedonia, Greece, Bulgaria, Romania, Moldova, Ukraine, Belarus, Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia, Turkey, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Russia It's a "cuckoo bumblebee" (subgenus Psithyrus): it produces only males and new reproductive females-no worker caste at all. Bombus rupestris is a cuckoo bumblebee (brood parasite) that invades nests of other Bombus species, kills or subdues the resident queen, and has the host workers raise its offspring. It is often associated with red-tailed hosts and is commonly referred to as the red-tailed cuckoo bumblebee. Queens are larger and more robust, built for nest invasion, while males are smaller with longer antennae. Both share the black body and red tail, so size and antennal proportions help sexing in the field.;
Aphids;Invertebrates;Red Aphids;This map shows the native origin of the Red Aphids. As a cosmopolitan species, they are now found worldwide. "Red aphid" is a color label, not a single taxon: many Aphididae species can be red/pink/orange depending on pigments, diet, season, and life stage. Aphids (family Aphididae) are small sap-feeding true bugs that often form colonies on plants. “Red aphids” is not a single taxon, many aphid species can be red/pink/orange due to pigmentation, diet, and life stage. They reproduce rapidly (often by parthenogenesis), excrete honeydew, and can transmit plant viruses. Sexual dimorphism occurs mainly in the seasonal sexual generation of many species: males are typically smaller and more slender, often winged, while sexual females are larger and oviparous. Many populations are dominated by parthenogenetic females, so sex differences may be absent for long periods.;
Tarantula;Invertebrates;Red Knee Tarantula;Adult size: typically ~12-15 cm legspan (female often larger-bodied), with bold orange-red patella ("knee") patches contrasting dark legs. A New World tarantula famous for orange-red 'knee' patches on the legs and a generally docile temperament, widely kept in captivity. Adult males are slimmer with proportionally longer legs and mature male palpal bulbs/tibial apophyses, and live far shorter lives. Females are larger-bodied with a broader abdomen and can live multiple decades. Spider;Invertebrates;Redback Spider;Adult female body length is typically ~10 mm, adult male ~3-4 mm-extreme sexual size dimorphism typical of widow spiders (Latrodectus). The redback spider is a venomous comb-footed spider (widow spider) native to Australia, notable for the female’s glossy black body with a red dorsal stripe. It builds irregular tangle webs and commonly lives around human structures. Adult female body length is typically ~10 mm, adult male ~3-4 mm-extreme sexual size dimorphism typical of widow spiders (Latrodectus). Females are glossy black with a dorsal red/orange stripe, males are paler (often brownish) with lighter markings and are frequently overlooked in the field.;
Facts;Invertebrates;Redback Spider Facts;Redback Spider facts for kids (and adults). This animal is part of the Active Wild Online Zoo : information, pictures and videos of all your favorite animals! The redback spider is a venomous spider that is mainly found in Australia. Although small, the redback can deliver a painful – and potentially deadly – bite. The redback spider is attracted to the warmth and shelter provided by human buildings. This means that they’re often found lurking in sheds, letterboxes … and outdoor toilets! Don’t forget to check under the seat! The female redback is significantly larger than the male (females can weigh up to 100 times more than males).;
Spider;Invertebrates;Regal Jumping Spider;Florida, Georgia, Alabama, Mississippi, Louisiana, Texas, South Carolina, North Carolina, Bahamas, Cuba Adult size is strongly sex-biased: females ~7-22 mm body length, males ~6-13 mm (reported in taxonomic treatments of Phidippus, e.g., Edwards' revisionary work). Phidippus regius is a medium-to-large jumping spider (family Salticidae) known for excellent vision, active hunting behavior (no capture webs), and frequent sexual dimorphism and color variation. Females are usually larger and show broader color variation (tan/orange/brown or dark morphs). Males are typically smaller, darker (often black), with sharper white markings and more conspicuous metallic chelicerae.;
Reindeer;Invertebrates;Reindeer;Norway, Sweden, Finland, Russia, Alaska, Yukon, Northwest Territories, Nunavut, British Columbia, Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, Ontario, Quebec, Newfoundland and Labrador, Greenland, Mongolia, China Adult size: shoulder height ~85-150 cm, head-body length ~162-214 cm, mass typically ~60-140 kg (females) and ~90-210 kg (males). A circumpolar deer species of the Arctic and subarctic, notable for both sexes typically growing antlers, strong seasonal migrations in many populations, and close ecological ties to tundra/taiga systems. In Eurasia it is widely herded (semi-domesticated) and commonly called reindeer, in North America it is commonly called caribou. Males are typically larger-bodied with heavier necks and substantially larger antlers. Females are smaller but usually antlered, antler growth and shedding timing differs, supporting winter foraging and social status.;
Flies;Invertebrates;Robber Flies;Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, Chile, China, Colombia, Germany, Egypt, Spain, Ethiopia, France, United Kingdom, Greece, Indonesia, Israel, India, Italy, Japan, Kenya, South Korea, Morocco, Mexico, Norway, New Zealand, Peru, Philippines, Poland, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Sweden, Thailand, Turkey, United States, Vietnam, South Africa Asilidae span a wide size range-roughly ~3 to ~60 mm long, from tiny gnatsized hunters to "giant" robber flies. Robber flies (family Asilidae) are predatory true flies that capture other insects (and occasionally small arthropods) in flight or from perches, using strong legs and a piercing proboscis to subdue prey. Sexual dimorphism is usually subtle and variable across the family. Males often show more conspicuous terminal genitalia and sometimes different bristle patterns or abdominal shape, while females typically have a broader abdomen for egg production.;
Beetle;Invertebrates;Rove Beetle;Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, Chile, China, Colombia, Germany, Egypt, Spain, France, United Kingdom, Indonesia, India, Iran, Italy, Japan, Kenya, South Korea, Morocco, Mexico, Malaysia, Nigeria, Norway, New Zealand, Peru, Philippines, Poland, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Sweden, Thailand, Turkey, United States, Vietnam, South Africa Staphylinidae is among the largest beetle families, with tens of thousands of described species worldwide. Rove beetles (family Staphylinidae) are one of the largest beetle families. They are typically elongate, fast-moving beetles with shortened wing covers (elytra) that expose flexible abdominal segments. Many are predators of other small invertebrates, others are scavengers, fungivores, or associates of ants/termites. Sexual dimorphism is common but not universal. Differences are often subtle externally (size, abdominal tip shape) and strongest in some groups where males have modified antennae, legs, or abdominal segments, genital differences are consistent but not always visible.;
Boa;Invertebrates;Rubber Boa;Adults are typically 38-84 cm total length, rarely reported to about 104 cm (Stebbins, Ernst & Ernst). The rubber boa (Charina bottae) is a small, nonvenomous boa distinguished by a smooth, loose-looking skin and a blunt tail that can resemble a second head. It is generally secretive, slow-moving, and considered one of the more cold-tolerant boas. Adults are typically 38-84 cm total length, rarely reported to about 104 cm (Stebbins, Ernst & Ernst). One of the most cold-tolerant boas: found from near sea level to about 3,000 m elevation in western North America (field guides/IUCN accounts).;
Facts;Invertebrates;Rusty Patched Bumble Bee Facts;This page contains rusty patched bumble bee facts for kids and students. This animal is part of our Endangered Animals series . A free printable pdf worksheet is available for this page. Click here or on the image below to download. (Answers can be found here .) The rusty patched bumble bee is a species of bumble bee endemic to North America. (‘Endemic’ means ‘only found in’.) As recently as the 1980’s it was a common species in the northeast and upper midwest regions of the USA and in southeast Canada. Since then, however, the rusty patched bumble bee’s population has experienced a severe decline .;
Bernard;Invertebrates;Saint Bernard;This map shows the native origin of the Saint Bernard. As a domesticated species, they are now found worldwide. The Saint Bernard is a giant domestic dog breed historically associated with the Great St Bernard Pass hospice in the Alps and famed for search-and-rescue lore. It is a heavily built, large-headed working-type dog kept today primarily as a companion and guardian. Males are typically taller, heavier, and more massively headed and necked, with a broader chest and heavier bone. Females are generally smaller and slightly more refined in head and body outline while keeping the same markings and coat types. The breed is named for the Great St Bernard Pass hospice in the Swiss Alps, founded in the 11th century.;
Shepherd;Invertebrates;Saint Shepherd;This map shows the native origin of the Saint Shepherd. As a domesticated species, they are now found worldwide. Saint Shepherds are mixed-breed dogs, littermates can differ greatly in size, coat length, and drive. The Saint Shepherd is a mixed-breed domestic dog typically produced by crossing a Saint Bernard with a German Shepherd Dog. Individuals vary widely but often combine large size with working-dog temperament, requiring training, socialization, and substantial exercise and grooming. Males are typically taller, heavier, and broader-headed, while females are more lightly built. Both sexes share similar coat types and color patterns, with considerable individual variability due to mixed ancestry.;
Sambar;Invertebrates;Sambar;India, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand, Lao People's Democratic Republic, Cambodia, Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei Darussalam, Indonesia, China Size: head-body length 1.62-2.70 m, shoulder height 1.02-1.60 m, tail 22-35 cm (field-guide ranges widely cited across its range). The sambar is a large deer native to South and Southeast Asia, known for its robust build, coarse dark coat, and (in males) sturdy antlers. It is one of the largest Asian deer species and is an important prey item for large predators in parts of its range. Males are larger and heavier-bodied, typically darker, and bear heavy 3-tined antlers, females are smaller, usually paler, and lack antlers. Males often show a more developed neck mane and throat ruff, especially in the rut.;
Crab;Invertebrates;Sand Crab;Argentina, Australia, Bangladesh, Brazil, Belize, Chile, China, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Egypt, Spain, France, Greece, Indonesia, India, Italy, Japan, Kenya, Sri Lanka, Morocco, Mexico, Malaysia, Mozambique, New Zealand, Panama, Peru, Philippines, Portugal, Singapore, Thailand, Turkey, Taiwan, Tanzania, United States, Venezuela, Vietnam, South Africa Mole crabs (Hippidae) are small decapod crustaceans that live on sandy ocean beaches, where they burrow in the swash zone. They typically filter-feed by extending feathery antennae into retreating waves and are common prey for shorebirds and fish. Dimorphism is usually moderate: females are often larger and carry conspicuous egg masses under the abdomen, while males tend to be smaller and slimmer. The strength of these differences varies among genera and species. Many species synchronize feeding with waves, filtering plankton from backwash using feathery antennae.;
Moth;Invertebrates;Saturniidae Moth;Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Cameroon, China, Colombia, Costa Rica, Germany, Ecuador, Egypt, Spain, France, United Kingdom, Greece, Guatemala, Indonesia, Ireland, India, Italy, Japan, Kenya, South Korea, Sri Lanka, Morocco, Madagascar, Mexico, Malaysia, Nigeria, Nepal, Panama, Peru, Philippines, Poland, Portugal, Russia, Thailand, Turkey, Taiwan, Tanzania, United States, Vietnam, South Africa The family includes some of the largest moths on Earth-wingspans can range from ~3 cm to ~25-28 cm in the biggest species. Saturniidae is a family of large moths commonly called giant silk moths (including emperor, royal, and moon moths). Many species have reduced mouthparts as adults and do not feed, living briefly to mate and lay eggs. Caterpillars are typically large and can be brightly colored or spiny, they spin robust silk cocoons. Sexual dimorphism is common but variable: males often have larger, more feathery antennae and are slimmer, more active fliers for locating females by pheromones. Females are frequently heavier-bodied with larger abdomens for egg production, sometimes with subtler antennae and pattern differences.;
Sauropoda;Invertebrates;Sauropoda;Antarctica, Argentina, Australia, Bolivia, Brazil, Canada, Chile, China, Colombia, Germany, Algeria, Spain, Ethiopia, France, India, Kazakhstan, Lao People's Democratic Republic, Morocco, Madagascar, Mongolia, Mexico, Mozambique, Niger, New Zealand, Peru, Portugal, Romania, Thailand, Tunisia, Tanzania, uk, United States, Uruguay, South Africa Sauropods ranged from island dwarfs ~6-7 m long (e.g., Europasaurus) to giants ~30-37 m and ~50,000-70,000+ kg (estimates vary, e.g., Argentinosaurus/Patagotitan). Sauropoda comprises the iconic long-necked, long-tailed, quadrupedal herbivorous dinosaurs, including some of the largest land animals known. They are part of the saurischian dinosaur lineage (within Sauropodomorpha) and were widespread during the Jurassic and Cretaceous. Scallops;Invertebrates;Scallops;Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, Chile, China, Egypt, Spain, France, United Kingdom, Greece, Indonesia, Ireland, India, Iceland, Italy, Japan, South Korea, Morocco, Mexico, Malaysia, Norway, New Zealand, Peru, Philippines, Portugal, Thailand, Tunisia, Turkey, United States, Vietnam, South Africa Many scallops have dozens to over 100 tiny blue-green eyes along the mantle edge, helping detect motion and approaching predators. True scallops (family Pectinidae) are marine bivalve mollusks known for radially ribbed fan-shaped shells and, in many species, the ability to swim by rapidly clapping their valves. They are widespread on continental shelves and are ecologically important filter feeders and prey for many predators. Many scallops have dozens to over 100 tiny blue-green eyes along the mantle edge, helping detect motion and approaching predators.;
Scimitar;Invertebrates;Scimitar;A large Saharan antelope historically widespread across North Africa, named for its long, slender, backward-curving “scimitar” horns. It is now extinct in the wild but survives in captive populations and has been the subject of reintroduction efforts. Sexual dimorphism is subtle. Both sexes carry long scimitar horns, males average larger-bodied with thicker horn bases and heavier neck/chest development, while females tend to be slightly smaller and more slender overall. Historically nomadic, tracking rainfall to exploit short-lived flushes of Sahel-Sahara grasses and herbs. Declared Extinct in the Wild by IUCN in 2000, large-scale reintroductions (notably in Chad) have rebuilt free-ranging herds.;
Bass;Invertebrates;Sea Bass;Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Belize, China, Colombia, Costa Rica, Egypt, Spain, France, Greece, Indonesia, India, Italy, Japan, Sri Lanka, Morocco, Mexico, Malaysia, Nigeria, New Zealand, Oman, Panama, Philippines, Portugal, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, Senegal, Thailand, Turkey, Taiwan, United States, Venezuela, Vietnam, South Africa Size range is extreme: from tiny basslets/anthias (~5-10 cm) to giant groupers up to ~270 cm and >400 kg. Common-name umbrella for multiple marine (and sometimes brackish) ray-finned fishes, which species is meant depends heavily on region and seafood-trade usage. Sexual dimorphism varies widely: many serranids are protogynous (female-to-male) with males larger and more territorial, while some (especially anthias) show brighter male coloration and longer fins. Some species show little external dimorphism outside spawning.;
Slug;Invertebrates;Sea Slug;Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, Chile, China, Egypt, Spain, France, United Kingdom, Greece, Indonesia, Ireland, India, Iceland, Italy, Japan, South Korea, Sri Lanka, Morocco, Mexico, Malaysia, Norway, New Zealand, Philippines, Portugal, Russia, Singapore, Thailand, Turkey, Taiwan, United States, Vietnam, South Africa "Nudibranch" means "naked gills," reflecting the exposed gill plume many species carry on their backs. Sea slugs are marine gastropod mollusks with reduced or absent external shells. The best-known sea slugs are nudibranchs (order Nudibranchia), celebrated for vivid coloration, specialized diets (often sponges, cnidarians, bryozoans), and diverse chemical/structural defenses. "Nudibranch" means "naked gills," reflecting the exposed gill plume many species carry on their backs.;
Spider;Invertebrates;Sea Spider;Sea spiders (Pycnogonida) are marine arthropods characterized by extremely long legs relative to body size, a reduced abdomen, and a piercing proboscis used to feed (often on soft-bodied invertebrates such as hydroids, bryozoans, and anemones). They are not true spiders (Arachnida), despite the common name. Sexual dimorphism is often modest in overall size and coloration, but males typically have well-developed ovigers used for grooming and carrying egg masses. Females may be larger in some species and usually lack ovigers or have reduced ones. Size spans extremes: trunk (body) often ~1-60 mm across the class, while leg spans range from a few mm to ~70 cm in the largest deep/polar forms. Many species have 4 pairs of legs (8 total), but some have 5-6 pairs (10-12 legs), reflecting major diversity within the class.;
Cattle;Invertebrates;Senepol Cattle;This map shows the native origin of the Senepol Cattle. As a domesticated species, they are now found worldwide. Senepol was developed on St. Croix (U.S. Virgin Islands) from N'Dama (West African taurine) and Red Poll (British taurine) cattle. Senepol is a tropically adapted beef cattle breed developed on the Caribbean island of St. Croix, best known for heat tolerance, slick hair coat, docility, and good maternal traits, it is a taurine (Bos taurus) breed rather than zebu (Bos indicus). Bulls are larger and more heavily muscled, with thicker necks and broader heads, while cows are finer-boned with a more pronounced udder and a generally lighter forequarter.;
Spider;Invertebrates;Sequined Spider;Australia, Brazil, China, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, Fiji, Guatemala, Indonesia, India, Jamaica, Japan, Kenya, Sri Lanka, Mexico, Malaysia, Panama, Peru, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Thailand, Tanzania, Vietnam, South Africa Adults across Thwaitesia are only a few millimeters long, commonly about 2-6 mm, with females often larger. Sequined (mirror) spiders are small comb-footed spiders in the genus Thwaitesia. They are noted for reflective, silvery abdominal patches formed by guanine plates that can appear like sequins. Like other theridiids, they build fine webs and are small insect predators. Females are generally larger with more rounded abdomens and more conspicuous reflective patches. Males are typically smaller, longer-legged, and show more developed palps, intensity and number of sequins can vary by species.;
Short;Invertebrates;Short;Sometimes called the spiny anteater, the short-beaked echidna (pronounced ih-KID-nuh) is found all over Australia and southern New Guinea. Short-beaked echidnas are one of two types of echidnas. The other type is called the long-beaked echidna. As long as there is a good supply of ants and termites, short-beaked echidnas can live in a range of climates and habitats. They are able to find shelter in rocks and fallen trees. Although they resemble porcupines or hedgehogs , and they do eat ants, short-beaked echidnas are not related to porcupines, hedgehogs or anteaters. They are actually a special kind of mammal called a monotreme.;
Shrimp;Invertebrates;Shrimp;Argentina, Australia, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, Chile, China, Germany, Egypt, Spain, France, United Kingdom, Greece, Indonesia, Ireland, India, Italy, Japan, Kenya, South Korea, Sri Lanka, Morocco, Mexico, Malaysia, Netherlands, Norway, New Zealand, Peru, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Portugal, Saudi Arabia, Sweden, Singapore, Senegal, Thailand, Turkey, Taiwan, Tanzania, United States, Uruguay, Vietnam, South Africa "Shrimp" is a common-name umbrella, not a single taxonomic group, shrimp-like decapods occur in multiple lineages within Decapoda (e.g., Caridea and Dendrobranchiata). Shrimp are small-to-medium aquatic crustaceans typically characterized by a laterally compressed body, a well-developed abdomen and tail fan, long antennae, and multiple walking/swimming legs. The common name covers several shrimp-like decapod groups and is widely used for edible species. Sexual dimorphism is common but variable: males often have modified swimmerets for sperm transfer, while females typically have broader abdomens or specialized pleopods for carrying eggs. In some shrimp-like lineages, females may be larger, in others, males have larger claws or ornamentation.;
Siberian;Invertebrates;Siberian;This map shows the native origin of the Siberian. As a domesticated species, they are now found worldwide. The Siberian Cat is a Russian landrace-derived domestic breed known for a dense, water-resistant triple coat and robust build. It is generally sociable and athletic, adapted to cold climates, and recognized by major cat registries as a pedigreed breed. Males are typically larger and more heavily boned, with a broader head and more pronounced ruff. Females are smaller and finer, though still muscular and substantial for a domestic cat breed. Their triple coat is water-resistant, with guard hairs, awn hairs, and a dense insulating undercoat.;
Tarantula;Invertebrates;Skeleton Tarantula;"Skeleton tarantula" is a pet-trade name inspired by the pale leg banding that can look like a skeletal pattern. Ephebopus murinus is a New World tarantula known for pale banding/striping that can resemble a skeletal pattern, hence the common name “skeleton tarantula.” It is a terrestrial to fossorial (burrowing) theraphosid and is sometimes kept in captivity. Adult females are larger and more robust with thicker legs and abdomen. Mature males are smaller and leggier, develop male palpal bulbs (mating organs) and often tibial apophyses, and generally live far fewer years after maturation. "Skeleton tarantula" is a pet-trade name inspired by the pale leg banding that can look like a skeletal pattern.;
Crab;Invertebrates;Snow Crab;Newfoundland and Labrador, Nouvelle-Écosse, New Brunswick, Quebec, Nunavut, Northwest Territories, Alaska, Greenland, Iceland, Norway, Russia, Japan A cold-water marine crab (a ‘tanner crab’) widely harvested in the North Atlantic and North Pacific and commonly sold as ‘snow crab’ in seafood markets. Males grow larger with proportionally longer legs and enlarged chelae, while females remain smaller with a broader, rounded abdominal apron for egg carrying. Mature males often dominate the largest size classes in fisheries. After the terminal molt, males stop molting for life-size is "locked in," while energy shifts toward mating and survival.;

Soldier beetles (family Cantharidae) are soft-bodied beetles commonly found on flowers and foliage. Adults often feed on nectar, pollen, and small insects, larvae are typically predatory in leaf litter or soil and can help control other invertebrates. Sexual dimorphism is usually subtle but common. Spider;Invertebrates;Southern House Spider;Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Louisiana, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Mexico Adult females are typically ~13-19 mm body length, adult males ~9-13 mm (males look leggier and slimmer). Kukulcania hibernalis is a crevice-weaver spider often encountered around homes, especially in the southern U.S. It builds a messy-looking, woolly silk tube/retreat in cracks and holes and waits at the entrance for prey. Females are larger-bodied and remain in tube retreats, males are smaller-bodied but longer-legged and wander, often entering homes. Spider;Invertebrates;Spider;Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, Chile, China, Colombia, Germany, Egypt, Spain, France, United Kingdom, Greece, Indonesia, Ireland, India, Iran, Italy, Japan, Kenya, South Korea, Morocco, Mexico, Malaysia, Nigeria, Norway, New Zealand, Peru, Philippines, Poland, Russia, Sweden, Thailand, Turkey, United States, Vietnam, South Africa Size spans extremes: some adult spiders are under 1 mm long, while the largest tarantulas can reach ~30 cm leg span. Spiders are arachnids in the order Araneae, characterized by eight legs, venomous chelicerae (fangs), and—uniquely among most terrestrial predators—the ability to produce silk from spinnerets for webs, prey capture, egg sacs, and shelter. They are globally widespread and highly diverse, with tens of thousands of described species. Sexual dimorphism is common but variable: females are often larger and longer-lived, while males are slimmer with proportionally longer legs. Males typically develop enlarged mating pedipalps and sometimes brighter patterns, spines, or tibial hooks used in courtship and mating.;
Beetle;Invertebrates;Spider Beetle;"Spider beetles" are mostly the Ptininae lineage within the family Ptinidae-relatives of furniture and deathwatch beetles. Spider beetles are small coleopterans in Ptinidae (most commonly the spider-beetle lineage, Ptininae) noted for their spider-like appearance: long legs, rounded abdomen-like body, and habit of scuttling in dim indoor environments. Many are scavengers and are frequent pests of stored products and dry organic materials. Sexual dimorphism is generally subtle across Ptinidae. Males often have relatively longer or more elaborate antennae and occasional leg modifications, while females may appear broader-bodied when gravid, definitive differences are frequently in genitalia. "Spider beetles" are mostly the Ptininae lineage within the family Ptinidae-relatives of furniture and deathwatch beetles.;

Sponges (phylum Porifera) are simple, mostly marine animals that lack true tissues and organs. They live attached to surfaces and feed by pumping water through a porous body, filtering out bacteria and organic particles. Lanternfly;Invertebrates;Spotted Lanternfly;The spotted lanternfly is a planthopper (a true bug relative) native to parts of Asia and widely known as an invasive pest in regions such as the eastern United States. It feeds on plant sap and can occur in large aggregations, impacting vineyards, orchards, and hardwood trees. Females are generally larger-bodied with a broader abdomen and visible ovipositor tip, males are smaller and more slender. Both sexes share the same wing coloration and spotted patterning. Each egg mass usually contains ~30-50 eggs, laid in rows and covered with a gray, mud-like waxy coating. Nymphs pass through 4 instars: early instars are black with white spots, the final instar becomes bright red with black/white patterning.;
Springbok;Invertebrates;Springbok;Both sexes carry horns (typically ~35-48 cm long), unlike many antelopes where females are hornless. The springbok is a medium-sized gazelle-like antelope native to southern Africa, famous for its characteristic “pronking” (high bounding leaps) and its role as a national symbol of South Africa. Males are generally heavier and carry longer, thicker, more strongly curved ringed horns. Females are typically slightly smaller and more gracile, both sexes retain the same high-contrast tan-white coat with the dark flank stripe. The Stabyhoun (Stabijhoun) is a versatile Dutch gundog breed originating in Friesland, historically used for small-game hunting, pest control, and as an all-around farm dog, today it is also kept as a companion and sporting dog. Beetle;Invertebrates;Stag Beetle;United Arab Emirates, Argentina, Austria, Australia, Bangladesh, Belgium, Bulgaria, Bolivia, Brazil, Canada, Switzerland, Chile, China, Colombia, Costa Rica, Czech Republic, Germany, Algeria, Ecuador, Estonia, Egypt, Spain, Ethiopia, Finland, France, United Kingdom, Ghana, Greece, Guatemala, Hungary, Indonesia, Ireland, Israel, India, Iraq, Iran, Italy, Jordan, Japan, Kenya, Cambodia, North Korea, South Korea, Lao People's Democratic Republic, Sri Lanka, Lithuania, Latvia, Morocco, Myanmar, Mongolia, Mexico, Malaysia, Nigeria, Netherlands, Norway, Nepal, New Zealand, Panama, Peru, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Pakistan, Poland, Portugal, Paraguay, Romania, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Sweden, Singapore, Slovakia, Thailand, Tunisia, Turkey, Taiwan, Ukraine, United States, Uruguay, Venezuela, Vietnam, South Africa Stag beetles (family Lucanidae) are a group of scarab-like beetles best known for the enlarged mandibles of many males, used primarily for wrestling rivals. Sexual dimorphism is often strong: males commonly have disproportionately enlarged, toothed mandibles and broader heads for wrestling. Females usually have smaller mandibles and a more compact head, overall body color can be similar but varies by species. Many species show strong sexual dimorphism: males often have oversized mandibles, while females have shorter, sturdier jaws.;
Insect;Invertebrates;Stick Insect;Australia, Brazil, Canada, Cameroon, China, Colombia, Spain, Fiji, France, Ghana, Greece, Indonesia, India, Italy, Japan, Kenya, Sri Lanka, Mexico, Malaysia, Nepal, New Zealand, Peru, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Portugal, Singapore, Thailand, Turkey, Tanzania, Uganda, United States, Vietnam, South Africa Phasmatodea includes both "stick insects" and the famously leaf-like leaf insects (family Phylliidae)-a whole order built around plant mimicry. Stick insects are insects specialized for camouflage, typically resembling twigs, stems, or leaves. They are primarily herbivorous and rely on crypsis, stillness, and slow swaying movements to avoid predators, some species also use chemical sprays or spines for defense. Sexual dimorphism is common but variable: females are often larger, heavier-bodied, and more frequently wing-reduced, while males tend to be smaller, slimmer, and more often winged and mobile. In some lineages the differences are subtle or reversed.;

Glider;Invertebrates;Sugar Glider;The sugar glider is a small nocturnal, arboreal marsupial known for its gliding membrane (patagium) that allows it to glide between trees. It is social and commonly forms groups, feeding on nectar, sap, insects, and fruit. Males are typically slightly larger and have obvious scent-gland development, including a bald or stained forehead spot. Females have a forward-opening pouch with teats, external coloration is otherwise broadly similar between sexes. Glides typically ~10-30 m between trees, longer glides around ~40-50 m have been reported in studies of Petaurus gliding performance. Reproduction is fast: gestation is about ~16 days, then tiny young develop in the pouch for ~60-70 days, litters are usually 1-2 joeys.;
Butterfly;Invertebrates;Swallowtail Butterfly;Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Cameroon, China, Colombia, Costa Rica, Germany, Egypt, Spain, Ethiopia, Finland, Fiji, France, United Kingdom, Greece, Guatemala, Indonesia, Israel, India, Iraq, Iran, Italy, Japan, Kenya, South Korea, Kazakhstan, Sri Lanka, Morocco, Madagascar, Mexico, Malaysia, Nigeria, Nepal, Panama, Peru, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Pakistan, Poland, Portugal, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Solomon Islands, Sweden, Singapore, Thailand, Turkey, Taiwan, Tanzania, Uganda, United States, Vietnam, South Africa Swallowtail butterflies are members of the family Papilionidae, a globally distributed group of often large, showy butterflies. Many species have tail-like extensions on the hindwings (the "swallowtail"), though some papilionids lack prominent tails. Sexual dimorphism is common but inconsistent across the family. Males are often brighter or more iridescent and may patrol or hilltop, females are frequently larger and may be duller or mimic distasteful butterflies, though some species show little difference. Family size spans some of the world's biggest butterflies (birdwings, Ornithoptera) with wingspans approaching ~25-28 cm.;
Scorpion;Invertebrates;Tailless Whip Scorpion;Argentina, Australia, Bangladesh, Brunei Darussalam, Bolivia, Brazil, Belize, Democratic Republic of Congo, Côte d'Ivoire, Chile, Cameroon, China, Colombia, Costa Rica, Cuba, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, Ethiopia, Fiji, Gabon, French Guiana, Ghana, Guatemala, Guyana, Honduras, Haiti, Indonesia, India, Jamaica, Japan, Kenya, Cambodia, Lao People's Democratic Republic, Sri Lanka, Madagascar, Myanmar, Mexico, Malaysia, New Caledonia, Nigeria, Nicaragua, Nepal, Oman, Panama, Peru, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Paraguay, Saudi Arabia, Solomon Islands, Singapore, Suriname, El Salvador, Thailand, Timor-Leste, Trinidad and Tobago, Taiwan, Tanzania, United States, Venezuela, Vietnam, Vanuatu, Yemen, South Africa Tailless whip scorpions (order Amblypygi) are arachnids characterized by a flattened body, raptorial pedipalps used to seize prey, and extremely elongated first legs modified as sensory “feelers” (antenniform legs). Despite the name, they are neither true scorpions nor venomous, they lack a tail and stinger. Often subtle to moderate and variable by lineage. Males commonly have longer, more robust pedipalps and sometimes longer antenniform legs, while females may have a broader, fuller abdomen when gravid, in some species differences are minimal. Their first pair of legs are "antenniform" feelers packed with touch and chemical sensors-used more like antennae than legs.;
Tarsier;Invertebrates;Tarsier;Tarsiers are among the very few primates that are obligate faunivores-living on insects and other small animals, not fruit. Tarsiers are small, nocturnal haplorhine primates famous for extremely large eyes, elongated tarsal (ankle) bones adapted for leaping, and a predatory, primarily insectivorous diet (they are among the few obligate faunivorous primates). Tarsiers are among the very few primates that are obligate faunivores-living on insects and other small animals, not fruit. Across the family, adults are tiny: ~9-16 cm body length, but carry long tails ~13-27 cm for balance while leaping.;

Caterpillar;Invertebrates;Tent Caterpillar;Armenia, Austria, Azerbaijan, Belgium, Bulgaria, Canada, Switzerland, China, Czech Republic, Germany, Denmark, Algeria, Spain, Finland, France, United Kingdom, Georgia, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Iran, Italy, Japan, North Korea, South Korea, Kazakhstan, Morocco, Mongolia, Mexico, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Russia, Sweden, Slovakia, Tunisia, Turkey, Ukraine, United States Across the genus, full-grown larvae are typically ~25-55 mm long, while adult moth wingspans are roughly ~25-50 mm (varying by species). Tiffany;Invertebrates;Tiffany;This map shows the native origin of the Tiffany. As a domesticated species, they are now found worldwide. The breed began in 1960s New York with two chocolate longhaired cats, Thomas and Shirley, owned by Jennie Robinson. Beetle;Invertebrates;Titan Beetle;Documented adult length reaches about 16.7 cm (mandible tip to elytra tip), among the largest living beetles. Titanus giganteus is a gigantic Neotropical longhorn beetle (Cerambycidae), famous for exceptional adult size and powerful mandibles. It occurs in northern South America’s tropical forests. Adults are rarely encountered, larval biology is poorly documented but likely involves wood-boring development. Males are usually more elongate with proportionally longer antennae and more robust mandibles, while females are broader-bodied with a wider abdomen for egg production. Overall coloration and surface texture are similar between sexes. Documented adult length reaches about 16.7 cm (mandible tip to elytra tip), among the largest living beetles.;
Titanosaur;Invertebrates;Titanosaur;Antarctica, Argentina, Austria, Australia, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, China, Colombia, Germany, Algeria, Egypt, Ethiopia, France, United Kingdom, Hungary, Indonesia, India, Italy, Japan, South Korea, Kazakhstan, Lao People's Democratic Republic, Morocco, Madagascar, Myanmar, Mongolia, Mexico, Niger, Peru, Pakistan, Portugal, Romania, Russia, Chad, Thailand, Tunisia, Turkey, United States, Uruguay, Venezuela, South Africa Across Titanosauria, estimated lengths range roughly 6-37 meters, spanning dwarf island forms to super-giants. Spider;Invertebrates;Trapdoor spider;Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, Egypt, Spain, France, United Kingdom, Indonesia, India, Italy, Japan, Kenya, South Korea, Mexico, New Zealand, Russia, Thailand, Turkey, United States, South Africa "Trapdoor spiders" aren't one species-several mygalomorph families worldwide build doored or turreted burrows. Trapdoor spiders are burrowing spiders best known for silk-lined tunnels capped by a camouflaged hinged door. Most are heavy-bodied, long-lived, ambush predators, often remaining near a single burrow and striking prey that passes the entrance. Males typically mature smaller and more slender, wander to find mates, and live far fewer years. Females are usually heavier-bodied, more sedentary, and remain burrow-based, often with longer overall longevity.;
Cricket;Invertebrates;Tree Cricket;Argentina, Brazil, Canada, Colombia, Costa Rica, Cuba, Dominican Republic, Algeria, Egypt, Spain, France, Greece, Guatemala, Israel, India, Iran, Italy, Morocco, Mexico, Tunisia, Turkey, United States Tree crickets (Oecanthus) are slender, mostly green or pale singing crickets in the true-cricket family (Gryllidae). They live on vegetation—trees, shrubs, and tall herbs—where males produce tonal chirps by rubbing forewings. Many species are identified by song patterns and subtle markings. Males typically have modified forewings for stridulation and may show clearer wing resonant areas. Females lack stridulatory structures and usually have a conspicuous ovipositor, overall size and color differences vary among species. Most species complete one generation per year, total lifespan often spans ~6-14 months including overwintering eggs.;
Dinosaurs;Invertebrates;Triassic Dinosaurs;On this page you’ll find a list of some of the best-known dinosaurs of the Triassic Period, together with pictures and facts on each dinosaur. The Triassic Period was the first period of the Mesozoic Era . It was during the Triassic Period that the first dinosaurs began to appear . They were mainly small, nimble animals that walked on two legs. There was little difference between them and their reptilian ancestors. During the Triassic Period, the dinosaurs were still to become the dominant land animals. Instead, it was a group of crocodile-like reptiles known as pseudosuchians that were the top predators . Both the pseudosuchians and the dinosaurs were members of a group of reptiles known as archosaurs . It wouldn’t be until the Jurassic Period – the period that followed the Triassic Period – that the dinosaurs would rise to dominance over their archosaurian cousins.;
Caterpillar;Invertebrates;Tussock Moth Caterpillar;Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, Chile, China, Germany, Egypt, Spain, France, United Kingdom, Greece, Indonesia, Ireland, India, Italy, Japan, Kenya, South Korea, Mexico, Nigeria, Norway, New Zealand, Philippines, Poland, Portugal, Russia, Sweden, Thailand, Turkey, United States, Vietnam, South Africa Erebidae is huge: adults range roughly 10-180 mm wingspan, showing extreme size diversity within one moth family. “Tussock moth caterpillar” refers to the larvae of tussock moths (subfamily Lymantriinae). They are typically hairy, often brightly patterned caterpillars that feed on leaves of trees and shrubs. Some species are important defoliators and many have irritating hairs that can cause rashes. Sexual dimorphism is mainly expressed in adults, not larvae: males are often smaller with strongly feathered antennae, while females can be larger and sometimes reduced-wing or flightless in some lineages.;
Cichlid;Invertebrates;Uaru Cichlid;Uaru amphiacanthoides is a large South American cichlid prized in aquaria for its disc-like body and social, generally peaceful temperament. Native to slow-moving Amazon basin waters, it is an omnivore with strong herbivorous tendencies and shows biparental care of eggs and fry. Sexual dimorphism is subtle. Males often develop slightly longer, more pointed dorsal/anal fin extensions and a more pronounced nuchal profile, while females are rounder-bodied when gravid and show a broader genital papilla during spawning. The species was scientifically described by Johann Jakob Heckel in 1840, during early Amazon ichthyology surveys. Juveniles are more heavily patterned with spots and bars, which fade as the adult "triangle" mark develops.;
Butterfly;Invertebrates;Ulysses Butterfly;Adults are large: wingspan typically about 10-14 cm, making it among Australia's biggest butterflies. Papilio ulysses is a large, iconic swallowtail butterfly noted for its iridescent blue upperwings and strong, gliding flight. It occurs in northeastern Australia and parts of New Guinea, frequenting rainforest edges where adults visit flowers and males patrol territories. Females are typically larger and show duller blue with broader black margins, while males display more intense, extensive iridescent blue. Sexes are otherwise similarly shaped, retaining the swallowtail hindwing outline. Adults are large: wingspan typically about 10-14 cm, making it among Australia's biggest butterflies.;
Moth;Invertebrates;Underwing Moth;Canada, China, Germany, Spain, France, United Kingdom, Italy, Japan, South Korea, Kazakhstan, Mexico, Poland, Russia, Sweden, Turkey, United States Across the genus, wingspans range roughly 40-115 mm, from modest underwings to very large forest species. Underwing moths (Catocala) are nocturnal erebid moths whose mottled forewings camouflage them on bark, while their brightly colored hindwings flash in flight to startle predators. Adults often hide by day on trees and visit lights or baits at night, larvae typically feed on woody plants. Sexes are usually similar in pattern, but males often have more feathery antennae for pheromone detection and may be slightly smaller and slimmer. Females commonly have a broader abdomen and can appear more robust.;

A small, brightly colored sesarmid crab popular in the aquarium hobby, noted for vivid eyes and semi-terrestrial lifestyle. It inhabits humid freshwater-margin environments and uses gills adapted for air exposure, spending much time on land near water. Bumblebee;Invertebrates;Vestal Cuckoo Bumblebee;Portugal, Spain, France, Belgium, Netherlands, Luxembourg, Germany, Switzerland, Austria, Italy, United Kingdom, Ireland, Denmark, Norway, Sweden, Finland, Poland, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary, Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, Montenegro, Albania, Macedonia, Greece, Bulgaria, Romania, Moldova, Ukraine, Belarus, Russia, Turkey, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Iran, Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia Adult female length about 1.8-2.2 cm, male about 1.4-1.7 cm (BWARS species account for Bombus vestalis). Snail;Invertebrates;Volcano Snail;Shell length reaches ~4.5 cm, making it among the largest known hydrothermal-vent snails (Warén et al., 2003). The scaly-foot gastropod is a deep-sea snail from Indian Ocean hydrothermal vents. It is famous for mineralized, armor-like scales on its foot and a shell often coated with iron sulfides, and for hosting symbiotic bacteria that provide much of its nutrition. Shell length reaches ~4.5 cm, making it among the largest known hydrothermal-vent snails (Warén et al., 2003). Lives at ~2,400-2,900 m depth on Indian Ocean hydrothermal vents (Central & Southwest Indian ridges).;
Walrus;Invertebrates;Walrus;Alaska, Nunavut, Northwest Territories, Quebec, Newfoundland and Labrador, Manitoba, Ontario, Greenland, Norway, Russia The walrus is a large Arctic pinniped distinguished by long tusks and sensitive whiskers used to find benthic prey. It forms social herds on sea ice and coasts, feeding mainly on clams and other invertebrates in shallow continental-shelf waters. Males are substantially larger and more robust than females, with thicker neck/shoulders and larger tusks. Mature males also show heavier scarring and more pronounced facial/neck thickening associated with display and dominance. They suction-feed clams and may consume roughly 3,000-6,000 clams in a day when conditions are good.;
Beetle;Invertebrates;Water Beetle;Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, Germany, Egypt, Spain, France, United Kingdom, Indonesia, India, Italy, Japan, Kenya, South Korea, Mexico, Nigeria, New Zealand, Philippines, Russia, Sweden, Thailand, Turkey, United States, South Africa "Water beetles" aren't one family-multiple beetle families independently evolved aquatic life in freshwater habitats worldwide. “Water beetles” is a broad common-name hub for beetles adapted to freshwater habitats. It includes multiple unrelated families within Coleoptera that have independently evolved aquatic lifestyles, ranging from active predators to scavengers and algae grazers, inhabiting ponds, lakes, streams, and marshes worldwide. Sexual dimorphism is common but uneven across aquatic beetle families. Males often have modified forelegs or antennae for mating, while females may show different elytral sculpturing or more rounded body shape, many species show little difference.;
Moth;Invertebrates;Wax Moth;This map shows the native origin of the Wax Moth. As a cosmopolitan species, they are now found worldwide. The greater wax moth is a pyralid moth whose larvae tunnel through honeycomb, feeding on beeswax, pollen, and hive debris. It is a major pest of stored comb in apiculture and a widely used laboratory model for insect immunity and host–pathogen studies. Dimorphism is subtle: females are typically larger-bodied with a fuller abdomen for egg production, while males are usually smaller and more slender, often more active in mate-seeking and wing-fanning behaviors near hive materials. At ~30°C, egg-to-adult development can take ~42-49 days, at cooler temperatures it may stretch for months.;

The Welsh Terrier is a small-to-medium terrier breed developed in Wales for hunting and vermin control. It is a domestic dog variant within Canidae, known for an energetic temperament and a wiry, often black-and-tan coat typical of many working terriers. Sexual dimorphism is mild: males are typically slightly taller, heavier, and broader in head and chest. Females are usually a bit finer-boned with a narrower skull, while coat pattern and texture remain similar.;

The West Siberian Laika is a spitz-type domestic dog breed developed in Russia for hunting (notably forest game). Tick;Invertebrates;Western Blacklegged Tick;Unfed adult females are about 0.30-0.37 cm long, males about 0.20-0.25 cm (standard ID keys, CDC/CPDH). Ixodes pacificus is a hard tick (Ixodidae) found primarily in western North America. It feeds on a range of vertebrate hosts across life stages and is medically important as a vector of several pathogens, including the agent of Lyme disease in parts of its range. Males are smaller with a scutum covering nearly the entire dorsum and show little engorgement.
